kinds.name: Agate
kinds.look: Drab brown, grey or black outside; often covered with small half-moon chips under 1 cm across; can be pitted.

kinds.name: Common opal
kinds.look: Glassy to waxy opal without play of colour, in seams, vesicles and cavities: milk white, yellow, brown, red, green or black (RI16 p.9); hyalite is clear and glassy, in botryoidal crusts (GIA 2015).

kinds.name: Jasper
kinds.look: Red, yellow, brown or green; rhyolite-margin jasper is "usually too fractured" (Bonnichsen).

kinds.name: Obsidian
kinds.look: Black to brown glass with a shell-shaped (conchoidal) break and razor edges; float pieces are often frosted or sand-etched (Lange 1965, Ore Bin 27(4)).

kinds.name: Precious opal
kinds.look: Thin layers and nodules in gas cavities, seams and joint fillings in rhyolite (Spencer: vugs "up to six inches", Broughton 1972 p.103); at Opal Butte, inside rhyolite geodes "from a few centimeters to well over a meter in diameter" (Smith 1988 p.230).

kinds.name: Star garnet
kinds.look: Rounded 12-sided (dodecahedron) or 24-sided (trapezohedron) crystals "from sand sized particles to golf balls or larger" (USFS 2026); most are under 2 cm (Evans & Moyle 2006 p.30).

kinds.name: Sunstone
kinds.look: Broken, glassy feldspar fragments with flat cleavage faces, mostly pea to thumb size: the smallest worth keeping "will not pass through a one-quarter inch screen"; pieces to 3 x 1.5 x 1 in (Peterson 1972 p.212).

kinds.name: Thunderegg
kinds.look: A ball from under an inch to 4 feet across, "most are about the size of a baseball", with "a knobby rind of drab, siliceous rock" (Staples 1965); found in the soil and loose rock near its source.

kinds.name: Topaz
kinds.look: Clear, pale yellow or pale blue crystals, short square-ish prisms with a flat end; in the Sawtooth small and glassy in the cavities with smoky quartz and pink feldspar; "colorless, and pale yellow prisms up to 7 mm.
